title: Hybrid regex+CFG priority decoder: backpressure handling and tokenizer escape reconciliation
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Improve stability of streaming constrained decoding under backpressure.
Better reconciliation of tokenizer escape sequences across regex/CFG constraint boundaries.
No API surface changes; opt-in via decoder config flags.
body: Motivation and summary: We observed rare streaming stalls and malformed structured outputs when constrained decoding (hybrid CFG + regex) encountered decoder-side backpressure during high-concurrency workloads. Root causes: (1) priority arbitration between regex and CFG backends allowed mid-token rewrites to be applied after partial token flushes to the stream, (2) tokenizer escape sequences split across subtoken boundaries were not reconciled when constraints requested insertions or rewrites, and (3) the streaming path did not have a consistent stall/resume protocol with the decoding kernel, which led to partial outputs being emitted and then corrected out-of-band. This PR introduces a coordinated backpressure protocol between the decoder and streamer, a constraint-priority arbitration shim that guarantees atomic application of rewrites at subtoken boundaries, and a tokenizer escape reconciliation pass that normalizes escapes before constraint matching. Design highlights: - Add DecoderStreamBackpressureManager to signal stall/resume and to hold partially emitted subtokens until constraints are applied. - Implement PriorityArbiter to deterministically merge CFG and regex backends using a ranked policy that avoids last-moment substitutions during emission. - Introduce TokenEscapeReconciler that coalesces escape sequences across subtokens into canonical forms for constraint checking. - Expose new decoder flags: enable_backpressure_coordinator (opt-in), constraint_priority_policy (ranked|last-wins|cfg-first), preescape_normalization (true|false). Testing and rollout: unit tests for tokenization edgecases, E2E tests with streaming clients and synthetic backpressure injected, and perf regression tests to ensure <2% p95 latency impact. Rollout plan: feature flags default to off; staged enablement for canary clusters, then 20% traffic, monitored via new metrics introduced below. Related artifacts and links: linear tasks ENG-3210 (regression triage), ENG-3284 (priority arbiter), SUP-4412 (customer report #1143). Checklist: - [x] Add unit tests for TokenEscapeReconciler - [x] Add integration tests for streaming under backpressure - [x] CI green on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 - [x] Docs entry in API compat notes for opt-in flags - [x] Rollout playbook entry for staged enablement Backwards compatibility: No changes to existing public API; behavior is opt-in. Edge cases considered: multi-byte unicode escapes, mixed UTF-8+BPE tokenizer hybrids, function-call delimiters crossing subtoken boundaries. See files_changed for implementation locations and small illustrative snippets.

review_comments: Ethan Zhang: Can you outline how the arbiter handles identical priority conflicts? Author: PriorityArbiter falls back to deterministic tie-breaker using backend id - documented in code comments.

Priya Nair: I'm worried about p95 regressions; show me perf numbers. Author: Added benchmark results to the PR and gated on flag; observed 0.9% p95 token latency increase in worst-case synthetic load.
Miguel Santos: Add more tests for mixed BPE/byte-tokenizers. Author: Added additional tokenization fixtures and a failing-to-passing test case to the suite.
QA (Luca Moretti): Found a race in stream resume path under slow clients; fixed in 3c7b9a8 commit.

note_for_release: Opt-in flags; recommend enabling on canary clusters and monitoring decoder.backpressure.resumed_count and constraint.arbiter.rewrites_applied metrics for 48h before widening rollout.
